title: Inventory Turns

articleSections.title: Inventory Turns: The Efficiency Engine of the Supply Chain
body: In the Private Equity world, Inventory Turns is the primary metric we use to assess the efficiency of a company's 'Physical' capital. It measures how many times a company has sold and replaced its inventory during a specific period. For an Operating Partner, high inventory turns (e.g., >8x for distribution) signify a lean, high-velocity supply chain that minimizes the amount of cash 'trapped' in the warehouse. Conversely, low turns suggest a bloated, 'just-in-case' inventory strategy that increases carrying costs and the risk of obsolescence. We view inventory turns as a direct lever for both EBITDA margin expansion and working capital improvement.

The math of Inventory Turns is a critical efficiency ratio: (Cost of Goods Sold in Period) / (Average Inventory in Period). If a company has $40M in annual COGS and carries an average inventory value of $10M, its inventory turns are 4.0x. This means the cash invested in inventory is recycled every 91 days (365 / 4). We use Inventory Management tools like Fishbowl or Oracle NetSuite WMS to track these turns at the SKU level, ensuring that we aren't just looking at a 'Blended' average that masks deep inefficiencies in specific product lines.

Operating Partners prioritize 'Working Capital Windfalls' by improving turns early in the hold period. If we can improve turns from 4x to 6x (reducing average inventory from $10M to $6.6M), we release $3.3M in permanent liquidity that can be used to pay down debt or fund an acquisition. This 'Cash Release' is often one of the highest-ROI initiatives in a 100-day value creation plan, as it requires no incremental sales and actually lowers the operating cost of the business. By professionalizing the inventory function, we transform a 'Storage' cost into a 'Velocity' asset.
articleSections.callout: Inventory Turns are the heartbeat of the physical business; the faster they spin, the more cash you generate.

articleSections.title: SKU Rationalization: The War on 'Dead Stock'
body: A common trap in mid-market companies is 'SKU Proliferation'—the tendency to keep adding new products without ever retiring the old ones. This leads to a 'Long Tail' of slow-moving or 'Dead' stock that consumes warehouse space and drags down the aggregate inventory turns. Senior Operating Partners insist on 'SKU Rationalization' programs that use ABC/XYZ analysis to identify the bottom 20% of products that contribute less than 5% of margin but consume 30% of working capital. We use NetSuite to automate this analysis and trigger 'Liquidation' events for non-performing SKUs.

The math of SKU rationalization is measured through 'Gross Margin Return on Investment' (GMROI). This metric combines margin and turns: (Gross Margin %) * (COGS / Average Inventory). If a product has a 40% margin but only turns 1x, its GMROI is 0.40. If another product has a 20% margin but turns 10x, its GMROI is 2.0. By reallocating warehouse space and capital toward the high-GMROI products, we can drive massive improvements in both profitability and cash flow. We view every square foot of the warehouse as 'Prime Real Estate' that must earn its keep.

We also analyze 'Inventory Aging' to identify 'Toxic' stock before it becomes worthless. Stock that has been sitting for over 180 days is a 'Red Flag' that requires immediate action. We implement 'Dynamic Pricing' and 'Bundle' strategies to move this slow-moving stock and convert it back into cash. By instilling a 'Zero-Stock' mindset for slow-moving items, we ensure that the warehouse is filled with 'High-Velocity' inventory that is mathematically likely to sell in the next 30-60 days. This discipline is what separates a professional PE operator from a founder who 'loves their products' too much to let them go.

articleSections.title: Just-in-Time (JIT) and Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI)
body: To achieve top-quartile inventory turns, a business must move toward 'Just-in-Time' (JIT) or 'Vendor-Managed Inventory' (VMI) models. In a VMI model, the supplier owns the inventory until the moment we use it or sell it, effectively pushing the 'DIO' (Days Inventory Outstanding) burden back up the supply chain. We use procurement platforms like Coupa to manage these supplier relationships and ensure that our JIT signals are accurately transmitted. This shift allows us to maintain high service levels while keeping our balance sheet almost entirely free of inventory risk.

The math of VMI is a 'Working Capital Game-Changer.' If we can move $5M of inventory from 'Owned' to 'Consigned,' our inventory turns effectively become 'Infinite' for that portion of the business. We look for 'High-Volume' commodities and components that are suitable for these programs. By partnering with our largest suppliers, we can create a 'Win-Win' scenario where they get better visibility into our demand and we get a 'Lean' balance sheet. This 'Structural' change in the supply chain is what drives sustainable multiple expansion at exit.

Operating Partners also look for 'Consolidation' opportunities in the vendor base. If we are buying similar products from 10 different vendors, our inventory is likely fragmented and inefficient. By consolidating spend with 2-3 'Strategic' partners, we can negotiate better JIT terms and lower 'Safety Stock' requirements. We use 'Digital Twin' simulations in tools like LLamasoft to stress-test our leaner supply chain against potential disruptions. By balancing 'Efficiency' with 'Resilience,' we build a supply chain that is a competitive advantage, not a liability.

articleSections.title: The Cost of Carry: Quantifying the 'Hidden' Inventory Tax
body: Inventory is not just 'Dead Cash'; it is an 'Expense Generator.' Carrying inventory involves 'Hidden' costs like warehousing, insurance, labor, taxes, and obsolescence, which typically run 20-25% of the inventory's value per year. For a company with $10M in inventory, the 'Cost of Carry' is a $2M-$2.5M annual headwind to EBITDA. By improving inventory turns and reducing the average balance, we don't just release cash; we directly increase the bottom line by eliminating these carrying costs. This is the 'Double Win' of inventory management.

The math of the 'Inventory Tax' should be socialized throughout the organization. We train warehouse managers and buyers to see a pallet of slow-moving goods as a $500/month 'bill' that the company is paying. We use 'Labor Tracking' modules in UKG to measure the exact cost of 'Touch Time' for moving and counting stale inventory. By quantifying these costs, we create the 'Economic Urgency' needed to drive aggressive turn improvements. This shift in mindset transforms the warehouse from a 'Cost Center' into an 'Efficiency Machine.'

Operating Partners also look at 'Inventory Accuracy' as a prerequisite for high turns. If your records are only 80% accurate, you will inevitably over-order 'just in case' to avoid stockouts. We implement 'Cycle Counting' and 'Barcode Scanning' using tools like Scandit to drive accuracy toward 99%+. High accuracy allows us to lower our 'Safety Stock' levels with confidence, which structurally increases our inventory turns. By professionalizing the basic 'Blocking and Tackling' of warehouse operations, we build the foundation for a high-velocity, high-value enterprise.

articleSections.title: Exit Readiness: Presenting a 'High-Velocity' Supply Chain
body: As we approach the exit, the Inventory Turns ratio is the primary evidence we use to prove the asset's 'Operational Excellence' to potential buyers. A buyer will be highly skeptical of a growth forecast that requires massive increases in working capital. We prepare for this by performing a 'Sell-Side Supply Chain Audit' 12 months out, creating an 'Inventory Bridge' that shows how we've improved turns and released cash through SKU rationalization and VMI programs. We use NetSuite data to provide a 'Clean Data' trail that proves our efficiency is structural.

Buyers pay a premium for 'Capital-Light' businesses. If we can show that we've increased revenue by 50% while keeping inventory flat, we prove that the business has 'Negative Incremental Working Capital'—a highly valuable characteristic that justifies a higher multiple. We highlight our 'Low Obsolescence' rates and 'High Accuracy' scores as proof of our management discipline. By de-risking the 'Physical' part of the business, we de-risk the entire deal for the buyer and ensure a competitive bidding process.

The final act is the 'Inventory Valuation Diligence.' We ensure that our 'E&O' (Excess & Obsolete) reserves are accurate and defensible, preventing any 'Surprise' write-downs during the buyer's audit. We use WMS data to show the buyer exactly how 'Fresh' our inventory is, with 90%+ having arrived in the last 60 days. By delivering a 'High-Velocity, Low-Risk' inventory story, we maximize the exit price and deliver a superior return to our LPs. In the end, fast inventory turns are the ultimate proof of an Operating Partner's success in building a lean, cash-generative machine.
